name: elevenlabs-arabic-tts-patterns
observations: Brand names: ALWAYS use English/Latin spelling inside Arabic text for multilingual v2
Comma pause trick: 'الفريق، من BrandName' forces clear pronunciation
Numbers: spell out years fully in Arabic words, add currency word after amounts
Warmth sweet spot: stability 0.35-0.40, style 0.35-0.40, similarity 0.70-0.80
Clean audio: bump similarity to 0.80 and stability to 0.40 to reduce artifacts
Speed: ALWAYS use native speed param (0.92-0.95), NEVER FFmpeg post-processing

name: elevenlabs-voice-agent-tuning-playbook
observations: CRITICAL: Never use response-by-response scripts (رد 1: X بس) — kills personality. Use situational guidelines instead.
CRITICAL: Never put exact-quote examples in prompts for voice agents — LLM will parrot them verbatim. Use 'express this idea your way' pattern.
Temperature sweet spot for Arabic voice agents: 0.5-0.7. Below 0.5 = robotic. Above 0.7 = incoherent.
TTS stability sweet spot: 0.40-0.50. Below 0.35 = noisy artifacts. Above 0.55 = monotonous robot.
Three-lever humanization: temperature + stability + prompt de-scripting. Apply all three simultaneously for best results.
Arabic numbers: ALWAYS spell out (خمس مية not 500). TTS engines cannot reliably convert digits to Arabic speech.
Brand names in Arabic: use English spelling (Seekapa) not Arabic (سيكابا). Arabic diacritics get swallowed by TTS.
Webhook tool JSON parsing: add explicit 'read the price field' instruction in BOTH tool description AND prompt. LLMs hallucinate prices otherwise.
After PATCH update: wait 30-60 seconds before testing. ElevenLabs propagation is not instant.
reasoning_effort: not supported for gpt-5-mini or claude-sonnet-4-5 in ElevenLabs. Set to null.
max_tokens 150 is good ceiling for Arabic conversation — prevents info-dumping while allowing complete thoughts.
Info-dump prevention: add 'لا تجمع كل المعلومات برد واحد' to prompt.

name: ux-ui-design-learnings
observations: 2026-02-02: Code-based React/TS prototypes beat static mockups for design assignments — evaluators can interact, iteration is faster, AI writes code faster than pixel-pushing
2026-02-02: Reviewer feedback maps directly to code changes — each feedback point becomes a specific file:line edit. Code-as-design enables rapid iteration loops.
2026-02-02: Subtle card separation (bg-white rounded-lg shadow-sm border border-gray-100) preferred over heavy borders or plain dividers for list items
2026-02-02: Typography hierarchy must be disciplined — section titles: text-base font-semibold, item titles: text-sm font-normal, metadata: text-xs text-secondary
2026-02-02: Icons should be minimal neutral base with soft color HINTS (muted: #9CA3AF, #A3B8CC, #9CB5A8) — not saturated colors, not all gray
2026-02-02: AI insights/explanations must be PROXIMATE to the content they reference — inline under summary banners, not floating at bottom
2026-02-02: Selection UX requires consistency — either all selected by default OR none. Never mixed. Always include Select All for bulk actions.
2026-02-02: Soft abstract illustrations at top of content areas create emotional warmth without distraction — use opacity-70, max h-[100px], centered
2026-02-02: Decorative visual indicators (colored lines, borders) must have clear meaning or be removed — reviewers flag meaningless ornamentation
2026-02-02: Scrollbar should only appear when content overflows — use overflow-y-auto with scrollbar-gutter: auto, never force-show scrollbar
2026-02-02: Consistent layout shell (same header + left nav) across ALL screens builds trust and professional feel
2026-02-02: Font consistency is non-negotiable — same family (Montserrat), same size scale, same weights across all screens including AI creation and input fields
2026-02-02: Parallel code-worker agents (6 agents for 12 fixes) work for independent UI changes — no merge conflicts when changes are in separate components
2026-02-02: Playwright screenshot + Gemini Vision audit is the definitive visual validation pipeline — scores of 95-98 confirm production quality

name: ux-ui-design-anti-patterns
observations: 2026-02-02: NEVER describe UI when you can show it — Or Project 2 first attempt failed because it was text-only. The research was excellent but zero visuals = fail.
2026-02-02: NEVER use heavy borders or strong card styling for list items — reviewer explicitly requested 'light shadow if it improves clarity, no strong borders'
2026-02-02: NEVER add decorative colored lines without clear meaning — vertical colored lines on unchanged items confuse users
2026-02-02: NEVER place AI explanations far from their content — bottom-of-page explanations are ignored. Inline them.
2026-02-02: NEVER use mixed selection states — some items checked, others not creates confusion. Pick one default.
2026-02-02: NEVER use inconsistent typography across screens — different fonts between AI creation and content screens breaks professional feel
2026-02-02: NEVER show scrollbar when content fits — unnecessary scrollbar is visual noise that degrades perceived quality

name: qc-v7-speaker-diarization-bug
observations: Project: qc-call-analyzer
Discovered: 2026-02-09
Status: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED, FIX PENDING
Symptom: 47-min Arabic call CA50058210 shows only 1 speaker (all labeled 'נציג') after V7.0 reprocessing

Root Cause 1 - Gemini Audio Timeout: _diarize_with_gemini_audio() must download 41MB file + upload to Gemini File API + wait for processing + generate_content() within 10-min Azure Consumption Plan activity timeout. For 45-min files this chain exceeds the limit.

Root Cause 2 - GPT Arabic Sentence Splitting: _detect_speakers_with_gpt() splits text with regex r'(?<=[.!?¿¡。،])\s+' which fails on Arabic STT output that has minimal punctuation. When <5 sentences detected, function aborts early (line 2484-2486).
Fix Plan A - Gemini: Either (a) split into separate download/upload and generation activities, (b) limit Gemini audio to calls <20 min, or (c) chunk audio before sending to Gemini
Fix Plan B - GPT Arabic: Add newline-based splitting for Arabic text in addition to punctuation regex. Arabic STT output uses newlines as segment boundaries.
Fix Plan C - Token limit: max_output_tokens=32000 may truncate 45-min transcript. Increase or process in chunks.
Affected calls: ~20/30 calls with LLM-based speaker detection (67% of calls with duration >2 min)
Key files: src/api/shared/durable_processing.py lines 2203-2408 (Gemini), lines 2419-2716 (GPT), lines 2723-2832 (activity_enhance_speakers)
SAS URL plumbing is CORRECT - 4-hour expiry, properly passed from prepare_audio to enhance_speakers
Status changed: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED -> FIXED AND DEPLOYED (V7.1)
Fix commit: cd6736d fix(pipeline): V7.1 Arabic speaker diarization for long calls
Fix 1: GPT Arabic sentence splitting - added newline-based splitting for Arabic STT output + Arabic question mark (؟) + lowered min sentences from 5 to 3 for Arabic
Fix 2: Gemini audio duration guard - skip Gemini for calls >20 min (1200s), falls through to GPT text-based detection
Fix 3: max_output_tokens scaled with duration: min(65536, max(32000, duration_seconds * 15))
Validation: CA50058210 (47 min) now detects 2 speakers (204 rep + 205 customer segments) via gpt_conversation method
Batch reprocessing: 33 affected calls from Jan-Feb 2026 triggered with force_reprocess=true

observations: [2026-02-20] 20-round hostile review trajectory: R1 63.8 -> R8 83.3 -> R14 93 -> R20 92.4 (multi-model calibrated). Score ceiling for well-reviewed codebase: 91-93/100.
[2026-02-20] Single-model score inflation: Claude Opus inflates ~4 points (95.5 single vs 91 multi-model median). NEVER trust single model above 90. Calibrate with 2+ additional models.
[2026-02-20] Optimal model count: 3 models for hostile review, 4 for final round only. 4th model adds <10% unique findings for 33% more cost. DeepSeek unreliable as primary scorer (63->93 swing).
[2026-02-20] Model personas: Gemini=stable baseline, GPT-5.2=harshest (if GPT approves, ship it), Grok=async/operational expert, DeepSeek=supplementary only.
[2026-02-20] Async migration is highest-risk refactor: R18 sync->async conversion broke 2 downstream callers, silently disabled security layer for entire review round via except Exception.
[2026-02-20] Documentation is 40-50% of interview score. Stale docs are WORSE than no docs. Cost 8-12 points per reviewer in R10.
[2026-02-20] Defense-in-depth compliance was unanimously praised across ALL 20 rounds by ALL 5 models. THE pattern for regulated domains.
[2026-02-20] State parity assertions at import time: rare defensive pattern that catches entire class of bugs. Praised by ALL reviewers as 'most production systems lack this'.
[2026-02-20] Review findings to FILES not parent context prevents context overflow. R6-R8 caused 3 overflows before this protocol.
[2026-02-20] Diminishing returns hit at R18. After that, fixes prevent score drops rather than raising scores. Ship when: no HIGH findings + model variance <3pts + remaining = trade-offs.

name: hey-seven-r46-learnings
observations: pip-compile --generate-hashes requires ALL deps in .in file — missing deps silently excluded from lockfile, making features dead code in prod
gcloud --to-latest and --to-revisions are mutually exclusive — combining them causes undefined behavior or CLI error
Sync redis.Redis in async code blocks event loop — use redis.asyncio or asyncio.to_thread() for all Redis I/O in async paths
Config fields that exist but aren't read at usage site = dead config — always grep for actual usage after adding settings
time.monotonic() has per-process epoch — meaningless cross-instance in Redis. Use time.time() for distributed timestamps
MagicMock auto-creates attributes returning MagicMock — breaks numeric comparisons (<=, >=). Always set numeric fields explicitly in test mocks
asyncio.to_thread() is the minimal-risk fix for sync-in-async — avoids full library migration to async redis

name: hey-seven-r47-gap-analysis
observations: CRITICAL LEARNING: Internal review score (96.7) vs external 4-model consensus (65) = 31-point gap
Root cause 1: Same-model self-review finds diminishing returns within same categories, not new categories of issues
Root cause 2: Incremental scoring credits deltas instead of absolute quality — calibration drifts upward over 45 rounds
Root cause 3: Calibration rule 'restore score if code didn't change' actively hides systemic issues found by fresh eyes
Root cause 4: Fixing a finding without validating the fix approach creates new bugs (R46 moved Redis inside lock per reviewer; R47 flagged lock+I/O as CRITICAL)
Root cause 5: 'Neutered tests' — disabling auth and semantic classifier in tests means production's most impactful paths have zero integration coverage
PROCESS FIX: After every 10 internal rounds or score >85, MANDATORY external multi-model gate (3+ models, different families). External consensus IS the real score.
PROCESS FIX: Retire calibration rule that restores scores when code didn't change. Fresh perspective finding new issues is not drift — it's discovery.
PROCESS FIX: asyncio.to_thread() for I/O libraries is ALWAYS wrong in async apps. Use native async clients. All 4 external models agreed.
PROCESS FIX: Warn-not-strip for unauthorized state mutations is TOCTOU. Guard-then-strip, always.
PATTERN: Internal scores are relative (progress tracking). External scores are absolute (quality assessment). Never confuse them.
